original_question: As in 17.57, let r(m) = {r + km | k ∈ Z} for integers 0 ⩽ r < m; for r1(m1) ∩ r2(m2) = ∅ let the class transposition τr1(m1),r2(m2) be the involution which interchanges r1 + tm1 and r2 + tm2 for each integer t and fixes everything else, and let CT(Z) be the group generated by all class transpositions. Let CTk be the subgroup of CT(Z) generated by the class transpositions τr1(k),r2(k) for 0 ⩽ r1 ̸= r2 < k. Since τr1(k),r2(k) permutes the residue classes modulo k, the group CTk is isomorphic to the symmetric group Sk. Let CT(k) = ⟨CT2, CT3,..., CTk ⟩. Is it true that for k > 3 the group CT(k) is isomorphic to the symmetric group SN, where N is the least common multiple of the numbers 2, 3,..., k?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.8 in the "New Problems" section of the 21st issue; Problem 17.57 is only the earlier source of the class-transposition notation and of CT(Z), not the target problem itself. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the intended problem almost verbatim: it defines the residue classes r(m), the class transpositions, the ambient group CT(Z), the subgroups CT_k and CT(k), includes the observation that CT_k is isomorphic to S_k, and asks exactly whether CT(k) is isomorphic to S_N for k > 3. That is precisely the content of Problem 21.8. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

For maximum sharpness, state the quantifier as "for every integer k > 3" and make explicit that S_N denotes the finite symmetric group on N letters, where N = lcm(2,3,...,k). ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let r(m) := {r + tm : t in Z} for integers m >= 1 and 0 <= r < m. If r1(m1) and r2(m2) are disjoint residue classes, let tau_{r1(m1),r2(m2)} be the involution of Z that swaps r1 + tm1 with r2 + tm2 for every t in Z and fixes all other integers, and let CT(Z) be the subgroup of Sym(Z) generated by all such class transpositions. For each integer k >= 2, let CT_k := <tau_{r1(k),r2(k)} : 0 <= r1 != r2 < k>; then CT_k is isomorphic to S_k because these generators permute the k residue classes modulo k. Define CT(k) := <CT_2, CT_3, ..., CT_k>. Is it true that for every integer k > 3, the group CT(k) is abstractly isomorphic to the symmetric group S_N, where N = lcm(2,3,...,k)?
justification: The draft is not trying to restate Problem 17.57 itself, whose question is about Out(CT(Z)); rather, it is targeting the later new problem, Problem 21.8, which explicitly starts from the 17.57 notation and then asks about the subgroup CT(k). Since 21.8 already repeats the needed definitions, the most faithful refinement is simply a cleaned-up, fully stand-alone version of that exact problem, without broadening it to other residue-class-wise affine groups or to neighboring CT(Z)-questions. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
